title: EU tech chief Virkkunen says AI rules can tackle rogue systems
key_facts: EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen told Reuters on Friday (9 Oct 2026) that EU rules can address the risks of rogue AI systems.
The AI Act, adopted two years ago, regulates AI by risk level and covers the whole lifecycle of AI models.
Regulators are giving companies guidance on evaluating their models and how long assessments need; a scientific panel of 60 experts will inform the process.
She rejected claims the rules are outdated, saying lawmakers required risk assessments, external experts and continued monitoring.

In late August the European Commission sent information requests to more than 30 AI companies about safety and security measures, then asked about transparency and copyright; the companies are not named and she is assessing the responses.
The requests could lead to investigations and fines of up to 7% of a company's global annual turnover; Chinese AI startups were also asked.
On a digital levy hitting big US tech firms, she said it is for EU governments, who are discussing new revenue sources for the 2028-2034 budget.
